Occurrences.Kwic: 塘水。師乃舉。洞山問雲巖。百年後忽有人。問邈得師真。向他道什麼。雲巖良久云。祇這是。山佇思。巖云。价闍梨。承當此事也大難。他後須是子細。山便辭去。後雲巖忌日。洞山掛真僧問。雲巖道祇這是。未審。還知有也無。山云。若不知有。爭解恁麼道。若知有爭肯恁麼道。師云。老婆心腸。蓋是養兒之道。衲僧手段。還他奪父之機。知恩報恩。句中宛轉。似肯不肯。量外提撕。箇是洞山底。或有人問普照邈得師真。對他道什麼。良久云。心不負人。面無慚色。上堂云。照與照緣。混融不二。心與心法。㳷合無差。所以道。如珠發光。光還自照。還會麼。百草頭上閑和尚。買盡風流不著錢。上堂云。雲斂長空風日和。太平樵牧共高歌。衲僧飯飽無他事。密密機前弄玉梭。所以道。

Occurrences.Kwic: 未微笑時會取；欲明安心之理，須向達磨未開口、二祖未斷臂時會取。於斯時節會得，猶較些子。若待世尊生下時，一手指天，一手指地，周行七步，目顧四方，自云：『天上天下，唯吾獨尊。』便已納敗闕了也。所以雲門大師云：『我當時若見，一棒打死與狗子喫，卻貴圖天下太平。』可謂將此深心奉塵剎，是則名為報佛恩。諸昆仲！其中還有知恩報恩者麼？若有，可請出來與吾相見；其或未然，可趁此手強腳健快須努力，決明此事，始不被天下老和尚舌頭瞞也。」良久，云：「會麼？相逢不飲空歸去，洞口桃花也笑人。」上堂。「諸昆仲！欲參博山禪，於未開口時會得，猶是落二落三了也。稍覺遲疑便合喫痛棒，又何待開口？縱能會得，堪作甚麼？豈不見？從門入者不是家珍，又安可為當

Occurrences.Kwic: 「昨夜降王宮，今朝成佛道，打破太虛空，如何覓得？」師云：「覓得覓不得且置，即今在什麼處？」僧喝一喝，師云：「只者一喝那？」進云：「亙古亙今藏不住，大千沙界絕羅籠。」師云：「為什麼腳跟不點地？」乃云：「今朝四月初八，淨飯王宮生悉達，九龍吐水沐金軀，大地山河光交潔，無端撞著老雲門，特地一棒要打殺。然雖如是，誰是知恩報恩者？若解知恩報恩，則三世諸佛、歷代祖師，總向汝一個鼻孔出氣，又說什麼未降王宮、度人已畢，未出母胎、說法已竟？只如今朝四眾臨筵，請山僧陞座，還是悉達降生了也？還是度人已畢？還是說法已竟？若檢點得出，許你具一隻眼。且道海雲為人一句又作麼生道？千峰勢到嶽邊止，萬派聲歸海上消。」喝一喝，下座。完經期，監寺偕兩序

Occurrences.Kwic: 。上座乃嘆曰：「我輩不見唐國知識將四百年矣，今日幸法駕光臨，得與瞻禮，豈非夙緣耶？敢求開示一言半句為金剛種子。」山僧因語之曰：「子能持此難遭希有之心，以明佛祖之道，不惟數百年前之開山面目猶在，抑今日承檀越之供養，則福有攸歸矣。子其勉之。」示大眾示大眾當此像季，身服田衣，宿生善因，極不容易。須要念德修德，知恩報恩，但以深究死生為第一件大事。不圖名，不苟利，除人我見，蕩生滅心，大小和睦，內外恭敬，有善相贊，有過相規，惟道是務，勿管是非，此謂之聖賢之聚會。不然，滴水粒米，無非鐵丸銅汁，可不畏與？當共勉之。示實歸禪人示實歸禪人世有虛頭禪，見他人病，極善開導。或云：一切放下，莫著於病。或云：四大本空，病將安寄？及自家熱病

Senses.Explanation: Know the kindness, repay the kindness. Hongzhi Zhengjue, raising the old Yunyan portrait-hanging exchange — Dongshan asked whether the one who said just-this still knows there is; if he did not know, how could he say it, and if he did, how would he consent to — appraises the old woman's heart as rearing a child and the monk's method as seizing the father's machine: know the kindness, repay the kindness — the phrase turns in the sentence, half consent half refusal, extra-measure prompting, and that is Dongshan's own. Dahui Zonggao, at the emperor's birthday hall, bows to the one who delivers all worlds — the golden wheel ruling the four continents, granting all beings peace — then demands: is there one who knows the kindness and repays it? and after a long silence answers with the calendar: of the year's three hundred sixty days, today alone is most auspicious. Yuanwu Keqin, blessing the sovereign — the whole earth receiving grace, dust-motes and lands all emitting the great treasure light — closes the hall on the formula: the one line of knowing-and-repaying, how does it go? No spirit fathoms the doing-of-nothing; everywhere the five-petaled flower fully opens. Tiantong Rujing, at the winter enlightenment-day, retells the six lost years, the eye lost beyond finding, the liar barely claiming the star — then rules that Cizhou Fangnian's praise of it is precisely what deserves the name know-the-kindness-repay-the-kindness, and if not, then a yearly bowl of tea on the eighth, with bows and incense, only dulls him. Wuyi Yuanlai, on the Buddha's birthday, lines up the birth, the seven steps, the one hand to heaven — already a defeat-mark — and Yunmen's declared one-stroke dog-feeding peace, calling it offering this deep heart to the dust-lands, just that named repaying the buddha's kindness, then demands of the assembly: is there one in this who knows the kindness and repays it? If so, come out and meet me; if not, while hands are strong and feet quick, settle this and stop being fooled by old monks' tongues. Jieweizhou Xingzhou, the same birthday elsewhere, asks who is the one who knows-and-repays, then rules that whoever resolves it draws the three-times buddhas and the successive patriarchs all to breathe through one nostril with him — no need for born-before-the-palace or taught-before-the-womb. Jifei Ruyi instructs his community that wearing the field-robe in this late age is no small karmic feat: remember the virtue and cultivate the virtue, know-and-repay, with penetrating birth-and-death as the one great matter — drop name and profit, and every drop of water and grain of rice is sweet; otherwise iron pellets and molten copper. And Yulin Tongxu, at the abbot's quarters of the repayment hall his donors built, names the radiant perfect fullness that everyone shades under, admits some have not yet known the kindness — the patrons and brothers now present are precisely the knowing-and-repaying ones, and must prove it at the tip of this monk's staff.
